newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodia, Burma, Laos await to join ASEAN - Hun Sen.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia, Burma, Laos await to join ASEAN - Hun Sen.

text.p: Cambodia's second Prime Minister Hun Sen said on Friday that Cambodia, Burma and Laos are ready and waiting for membership of the Association of Southeast Asian nations.

Hun Sen made the comments in Thailand after arriving from a three-day visit to Burma. He said he was pleased with his meeting with leaders of Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council but did not give details of their talks.
"...We did not discuss whether we should join or not join ASEAN but we, Cambodia, Burma and Laos, are ready to join ASEAN together," Hun Sen said.
"We are preparing and are waiting only for the D-day (to join)," he added.
The three nations are currently observers to the seven-nation regional grouping and hope to become full members this year.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Hun Sen, who is due to meet Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Saturday, also said Phnom Penh had decided to end what he called the "logging anarchy" of Thai businessmen.

"Both prime minister Prince (Norodom) Ranariddh and myself have determined and decided that there will be no more. We do not want to reopen this logging anarchy," he said when asked about logging deals with Thailand.
The Cambodian government has accused Thai businessmen of violating its order banning logging, charging that fresh-cut logs were still finding their way into Thailand until the end of 1996.
Cambodia's logging ban has sparked complaints from Thai businessmen who say they had bought millions of cubic metres of wood from Cambodia and that the wood is stranded in that country.
The London-based environmental group Global Witness has accused the Thai government of taking bribes to allow the hauling of Cambodian logs.
